behavioral_analysis.description: Trailing stop fires at 89.9% loss rate. This means positions briefly moved enough to ACTIVATE the trailing stop mechanism, then reversed before reaching profit target. The trailing stop distance (inferred ~60 bps from prior audit) is too tight relative to symbol volatility, causing whipsaw exits.
evidence: WR at TS exit = 10.1% (vs 30.39% overall WR)
Average hold at TS loss = 1,842s — positions held long enough to activate TS
TIER_2_TAKE_PROFIT has WR=100% and avg_pnl=+$1.37 — TP-eligible moves exist
Max hold at TS win suggests small wins occur when stop placed very tight

comparison_with_tp.finding: If TS were removed and replaced with wider TP, system might convert 355 TS-losses to TP-wins or extended hold gains

counterfactual.scenario_A: If trailing stop widened from 60 to 120 bps: fewer premature TS exits, more TP and MHT exits — estimated +$50-100 PnL improvement (unverified, requires replay)
counterfactual.scenario_B: If trailing stop removed entirely: WR would likely rise above 50% (355 TS losses become open positions), but tail risk increases significantly
counterfactual.scenario_C: ATR-based trailing stop: adjusts to symbol volatility — requires 100+ trade validation per symbol/TF

remediation_required: Widen trailing stop distance from ~60 bps to 100-150 bps on 1m/5m
Run 200-trade soak after any TS parameter change before live approval
Add per-trade MFE/MAE recording to quantify optimal stop distance
confidence: CONFIRMED — computed from 645 closed trade records
